text:
Montreal arrives with points in five straight (4-0-1) but a sour taste from Tuesday, when Winnipeg came back from four goals down to win 5-4 in overtime and end the Canadiens' win streak at five. They're still without Ivan Demidov and Mike Matheson, though Nick Suzuki is off the out list and day-to-day. Utah is 3-2-0 in its last five, coming off a 3-2 win in Toronto, and is missing John Marino, with Mikhail Sergachev now up to 25:22 a night.

Our numbers favor the visitors on the ice. At five on five, UTA has taken 59% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) against 52% for MTL, and our model projects 3.39 to 3.03 for Utah. Montreal's wins have come despite getting only 48% of the chances in its last five. The special teams matchup is the one to watch: Utah's power play creates 0.79 expected goals a game, Montreal's penalty kill allows 0.85, and the Canadiens take 5.2 penalties a game.

In net, projected starter Jacob Fowler is +9.7 goals saved above expected this season, which measures how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots called for. Karel Vejmelka is at -6.8 after a +5.4 year in 2025-26. Cole Caufield (37% to score) and Suzuki (73% for a point) lead Montreal. For Utah, Logan Cooley has 12 points in 10 games and Clayton Keller plays his 700th NHL game. Our under-the-radar pick is Anders Lee, a third-liner at about 14:19 a night with 2.5 expected goals in his last 10. We have him at 22% to score, a player to watch.
